title: Enhancing import map handling in conjunction with a strict CSP

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Many (single page) apps should make use of a framework hosted on a CDN. The module references in the apps should be independent of the version, concrete location, and inner structure of the framework. Thus, an import map is required for mapping the references contained in the modules of the apps to the actual locations of the required modules on the CDN. To allow switching the framework versions without changing the apps (for following patch versions of the framework) or with modifying only a single entry point URL (for following minor versions), the information contained in the import map should be stored with the framework itself on the CDN.

At the same time, it must be possible to use a strict CSP (Content Security Policy), i. e. one that does not have `unsafe-inline` in their (effective) `script-src` directive. With https://github.com/WICG/import-maps/issues/105, import maps have been put under CSP control. As import maps require an inline `<script type="importmap“>` (external import maps are not supported by the standard / browsers) , nonces or hashes need to be used to enable the usage of such import maps as of today. Using nonces / hashes however requires additional dynamics (see the next question) that adds additional complexity.

### What solutions exist today?

* Inline with nonce: This requires dynamic app serving to generate the nonce. The nonce then needs to be made available to inject the import map into the HTML document. While the dynamic app serving adds complexity, the nonce handling has the potential to reduce the security. 
* Inline with hash: This requires that the hashes (per framework version) are included in the HTTP response. So,  either the HTTP server needs to fetch the hashes from the CDN, or the apps need to be rebuild, whenever a new framework version (even patches) is to be used. This adds complexity on the app serving side, as well as on the framework side (for calculating the hashes).

### How would you solve it?

There are already some solution proposals for this, but none has been implemented:
* https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8355: Allow an external import map via a src attribute (`<script type="importmap" src="/importmap.json"></script>`). This would be quite easy from a usage perspective and requires no changes on CSP side. Browser implementation-wise this might look different. Expectation here is that this also works when dynamically inserting the import map element.
* https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12217: Allow for non-DOM handling of import maps. This should also be easy to use, if import maps handled via this API are not limited via the CSP inline script handling. It might even be better, as the mapping information could be bundled together with the injecting code in one JS file (e.g. generated during build time).

If the previous two proposals are not likely to be implemented soon, I can propose the following alternative: 
* While CSP prevents the usage of inline styles in the HTML document if no `unsafe-inline` is specified in the (effective) `style-src`directive, it is possible to use the corresponding DOM API (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) to add inline styles.
* Similarly, CSP checks could be skipped if an inline script element for an import map that has been created via JavaScript is added to the DOM.
* Implementation effort:
  * Tag script element if created via JS API
  * Untag script element, if taken out of the DOM or modified via DOM content manipulation
  * Skip CSP check for tagged inline script elements of type `importmap`
* Usage effort: Straight forward: Add import maps (e.g. by apps or framework) as required
* Initial security reasoning
  * Import maps originating from HTML parsing are still not possible.
  * JS code still can only create import map content when creating an import map.
  * The target modules specified in the import map are still covered by CSP checks.

There are some more options that look not so promising to me
* https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12164: Having links or other HTTP headers to add import maps also seems not to be an ideal solution. On the standard / implementation side, this looks like quite some effort and raises security questions (e.g. who is allowed to contribute which import maps?). On the usage side, the app and/or the CDN server need to generate these HTTP headers, adding complexity.
* CSP could be extended by a special source for inline import maps. However, this would make CSP more complex for a single use case.


### Anything else?

_No response_
